Major_Awards: FIPRESCI Prize and Best Director at Cannes; Grand Prize of the Cinema of Creation; Tarkovsky's penultimate masterpiece

Title: Parenthood
Synopsis: An extended family navigates the joys and disasters of raising children across three generations with humor warmth and anxiety.
Major_Awards: 2 Oscar noms; $100M domestic; Steve Martin; one of the most relatable family comedies ever made

Title: RoboCop
Synopsis: A brutally murdered Detroit police officer is resurrected as a cyborg law enforcer and struggles to reclaim his humanity and identity.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Sound Effects Editing; 2 noms; National Film Registry; Saturn Award; razor-sharp corporate satire

Title: Round Midnight
Synopsis: An aging American jazz saxophonist in 1950s Paris finds an unlikely savior in a devoted French fan who helps him reclaim his music and dignity.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Original Score (Herbie Hancock); Dexter Gordon Oscar-nominated Best Actor; Cesar Award

Title: Tron
Synopsis: A computer programmer is digitized and transported into a virtual world where he must compete in gladiatorial games to survive and escape.
Major_Awards: Pioneered computer-generated imagery in film; 2 Oscar noms; cult classic; visually revolutionary though commercially underperforming

Title: Educating Rita
Synopsis: A working-class hairdresser enrolls in an Open University literature course and her intellectual awakening transforms both her and her jaded tutor.
Major_Awards: BAFTA Best Actor/Actress; 3 BAFTA wins; Golden Globe Best Actor/Actress (Musical/Comedy); Michael Caine/Julie Walters

Title: Full Metal Jacket
Synopsis: Marine recruits endure dehumanizing boot camp under a sadistic drill instructor before facing the chaos and moral void of the Vietnam War.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom for Best Adapted Screenplay; National Film Registry; one of the defining Vietnam War films

Title: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom
Synopsis: Indiana Jones crash-lands in India and discovers a village enslaved by a Thuggee cult that has stolen a sacred stone and kidnapped the children.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects; $179M domestic; led directly to creation of PG-13 rating

Title: The Color of Money
Synopsis: An aging pool hustler mentors a cocky young player on the road to a major tournament but finds himself drawn back into competition.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Actor (Paul Newman first career win); Tom Cruise co-star; Scorsese directing; Newman long-overdue recognition

Title: Under the Volcano
Synopsis: A British diplomat drinking himself to death in 1930s Mexico relives his failures in love and life on the Day of the Dead.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom for Best Actor (Albert Finney); based on Malcolm Lowry's masterpiece; John Huston powerful adaptation

Title: El Norte
Synopsis: A Guatemalan brother and sister flee political persecution and make a perilous journey to the United States seeking a better life.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom for Best Original Screenplay; National Film Registry; American Playhouse; landmark of Latin American cinema in the US

Title: The Name of the Rose
Synopsis: A Franciscan friar investigates a series of murders at a medieval Italian abbey where a forbidden book holds the key to the deadly mystery.
Major_Awards: Cesar Award Best Foreign Film; BAFTA nom; based on Umberto Eco's bestselling novel; Sean Connery starring

Title: The Empire Strikes Back
Synopsis: The Rebel Alliance faces devastating setbacks as Darth Vader pursues Luke Skywalker who trains with Jedi Master Yoda and confronts a shattering revelation.
Major_Awards: Won 2 Oscars (Sound, Special Achievement); 3 noms; $209M domestic; National Film Registry; AFI Top 100

Title: The King of Comedy
Synopsis: An aspiring stand-up comedian kidnaps a late-night talk show host to secure a spot on the show in this prophetic satire of celebrity obsession.
Major_Awards: BAFTA nomination; initially underappreciated; now widely regarded as one of Scorsese's greatest and most prescient films

Title: The Little Mermaid
Synopsis: A mermaid princess trades her voice for human legs to pursue the prince she loves in this musical fairy tale that launched the Disney Renaissance.
Major_Awards: Won 2 Oscars (Original Score, Original Song); 3 noms; $84M domestic; revitalized Disney animation singlehandedly

Title: 9 to 5
Synopsis: Three female office workers kidnap their sexist boss and run the company themselves implementing progressive reforms with hilarious results.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom for Best Original Song; $103M domestic; iconic feminist comedy; Dolly Parton/Jane Fonda/Lily Tomlin

Title: An American Werewolf in London
Synopsis: Two American backpackers are attacked by a werewolf on the English moors and the survivor begins a horrifying transformation in London.
Major_Awards: Won inaugural Oscar for Best Makeup (Rick Baker); revolutionary practical effects; National Film Registry

Title: Babettes Feast
Synopsis: A French refugee works as a cook for two elderly Danish sisters for fourteen years before spending her lottery winnings on one magnificent feast.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film; considered one of the greatest food films ever made

Title: Back to the Future
Synopsis: A teenager accidentally travels to 1955 in a time-traveling DeLorean and must ensure his parents fall in love or risk erasing his own existence.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Film Editing; $210M domestic; AFI Top 100; National Film Registry; Hugo Award

Title: Beetlejuice
Synopsis: A recently deceased couple haunting their former home hire an obnoxious freelance bio-exorcist to scare away the insufferable new owners.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Makeup; $73M domestic on $15M budget; defined Tim Burton's gothic aesthetic; National Film Registry

Title: Bull Durham
Synopsis: A veteran catcher mentors a wild young pitcher on a minor league baseball team while competing for the affections of a devoted baseball groupie.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom for Best Original Screenplay; National Film Registry; widely considered the greatest baseball movie ever made

Title: Crocodile Dundee
Synopsis: An American journalist lures a rugged Australian bushman to New York City where his outback skills create hilarious culture-clash situations.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom; $174M domestic; highest-grossing Australian film of all time at that point; cultural phenomenon

Title: Diner
Synopsis: A group of young men in 1959 Baltimore cling to their late-night diner hangout as adulthood threatens to pull them apart.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom for Best Original Screenplay; National Film Registry; launched careers of Rourke Barkin Guttenberg Stern

Title: Dirty Dancing
Synopsis: A sheltered teenager falls for a working-class dance instructor during a 1963 family vacation at a Catskills resort.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Original Song (I've Had the Time of My Life); $64M domestic on $5M budget; massive cultural phenomenon

Title: Drugstore Cowboy
Synopsis: A crew of junkies in 1970s Portland rob pharmacies to feed their habits in this unflinchingly honest and darkly humorous addiction drama.
Major_Awards: Independent Spirit Award Best Film/Director/Actor; NY Film Critics Best Film; launched Gus Van Sant's career
Key_Sources: Independent Spirit Awards; NY Film Critics

Title: Flashdance
Synopsis: A Pittsburgh steel welder by day and exotic dancer by night dreams of attending a prestigious dance conservatory against all odds.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Original Song (What a Feeling); $92M domestic; cultural phenomenon of the early 1980s

Title: Heathers
Synopsis: A disillusioned teenager and her sociopathic new boyfriend begin murdering the popular kids at their high school and disguising the deaths as suicides.
Major_Awards: Cult classic that subverted the teen film genre; Independent Spirit nom; massive cultural influence

Title: My Neighbor Totoro
Synopsis: Two young sisters discover magical forest spirits including the gentle giant Totoro after moving to the countryside to be near their ailing mother.
Major_Awards: Kinema Junpo Best Film; Mainichi Film Award; considered one of the greatest animated films ever made; Studio Ghibli landmark

Title: Purple Rain
Synopsis: A young musician in Minneapolis struggles with a turbulent home life and a rival band while pursuing stardom and love.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Original Song Score; $68M domestic; Prince iconic performance; soundtrack sold 25M copies worldwide

Title: Repo Man
Synopsis: A young punk rocker becomes a car repossessor in Los Angeles and gets caught up in the search for a mysterious Chevy Malibu with something alien in the trunk.
Major_Awards: National Film Registry; Independent Spirit Award nom; cult classic that defined 1980s underground cinema

Title: River's Edge
Synopsis: When a teenager murders his girlfriend and shows the body to his friends the group's disturbing indifference reveals a generation's moral paralysis.
Major_Awards: Independent Spirit Award Best Film; one of the most disturbing and critically acclaimed indie films of the decade

Title: Splash
Synopsis: A young man falls in love with a woman who turns out to be a mermaid in this charming romantic fantasy that launched Tom Hanks' comedy career.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom for Best Original Screenplay; $69M domestic; Ron Howard breakout; Touchstone Pictures first release

Title: Starman
Synopsis: An alien takes the form of a young widow's dead husband and she reluctantly drives him across the country to his rendezvous point.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom for Best Actor (Jeff Bridges); John Carpenter's most tender film; Karen Allen co-stars

Title: Stranger Than Paradise
Synopsis: A disaffected New York hipster reluctantly hosts his Hungarian cousin before the two embark on an aimless trip to Cleveland and Florida.
Major_Awards: Won Camera d'Or at Cannes; National Society of Film Critics Best Film; landmark of American independent cinema
Key_Sources: Cannes Film Festival; National Society of Film Critics

Title: The Abyss
Synopsis: A civilian diving team is recruited to help recover a lost nuclear submarine and encounters mysterious alien beings in the ocean depths.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects; pioneered CGI water effects; James Cameron's most underrated work

Title: The Accused
Synopsis: A young woman who was gang-raped in a bar fights for justice when the prosecution accepts a lesser plea deal for her attackers.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Actress (Jodie Foster); powerful and controversial examination of sexual assault and victim-blaming

Title: The Fly
Synopsis: A brilliant but eccentric scientist accidentally merges his DNA with a housefly during a teleportation experiment and undergoes a horrifying transformation.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Makeup; Saturn Award; one of the greatest body horror films ever made

Title: The Karate Kid
Synopsis: A bullied teenager learns karate and life lessons from an unassuming Japanese handyman who turns out to be a martial arts master.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom for Best Supporting Actor (Pat Morita); $91M domestic; Cultural phenomenon; AFI Top 100 Cheers

Title: The Official Story
Synopsis: An upper-class Argentine history teacher gradually realizes that her adopted daughter may have been stolen from political dissidents during the Dirty War.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film; first Argentine film to win Oscar; powerful political cinema

Title: The Princess Bride
Synopsis: A grandfather reads his sick grandson a fairytale of fencing giants miracles and true love that becomes a perfectly witty adventure of its own.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom; National Film Registry; became one of the most beloved and quoted films of all time

Title: The Trip to Bountiful
Synopsis: An elderly woman trapped in a tiny apartment with her domineering daughter-in-law makes one last escape to visit her childhood home.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Actress (Geraldine Page); heartbreaking and gentle; Geraldine Page's crowning achievement

Title: The Year of Living Dangerously
Synopsis: A young Australian journalist in 1965 Indonesia navigates political upheaval and a dangerous love affair as Sukarno's regime crumbles.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Supporting Actress (Linda Hunt); Peter Weir's international breakthrough alongside Gallipoli

Title: Top Gun
Synopsis: A cocky young naval aviator competes at the elite Fighter Weapons School while dealing with rivalry romance and the ghost of his father's legacy.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Original Song; $176M domestic; highest-grossing film of 1986; cultural phenomenon

Title: Wall Street
Synopsis: An ambitious young stockbroker is seduced into the world of insider trading by a ruthless corporate raider whose mantra is greed is good.
Major_Awards: Won Oscar for Best Actor (Michael Douglas); defined 1980s excess and corporate culture

Title: When Harry Met Sally
Synopsis: Two friends debate whether men and women can be friends without sex complicating things over twelve years of chance encounters.
Major_Awards: Oscar nom for Best Original Screenplay (Nora Ephron); AFI Top 100 Laughs; $92M domestic; iconic deli scene

Title: Fitzcarraldo
Synopsis: An opera-obsessed dreamer attempts to haul a steamship over a mountain in the Peruvian jungle to fund an opera house in the Amazon.
Major_Awards: Won Best Director at Cannes; the production itself became legendary; Werner Herzog's most ambitious undertaking

Title: Kiki's Delivery Service
Synopsis: A thirteen-year-old witch leaves home to spend a year alone in a new city and sets up a delivery service using her broomstick in this Miyazaki masterpiece about independence, self-doubt, and the rediscovery of lost confidence.

Title: Landscape in the Mist
Synopsis: A greek girl and her little brother travel across a wintry Greece searching for the father they have never met in Theo Angelopoulos's lyrical and heartbreaking road movie about childhood innocence and the cruelty of the real world.

Title: Local Hero
Synopsis: An American oil company executive is sent to buy a Scottish coastal village for a refinery but falls under the spell of its eccentric inhabitants.
Major_Awards: BAFTA Best Direction; Mark Knopfler score; one of the most charming British films of the decade

Title: Love Streams
Synopsis: A free-spirited woman going through a painful divorce seeks refuge with her emotionally withdrawn brother in this deeply personal Cassavetes film about two people whose capacity for love vastly exceeds their ability to connect with the world.

Title: Mishima: A Life in Four Chapters
Synopsis: The life of Japanese author Yukio Mishima is told through four interwoven chapters blending biography and dramatizations of his novels.
Major_Awards: Won Best Artistic Contribution at Cannes; Philip Glass score; one of the most formally ambitious biopics ever made

Title: Once Upon a Time in America
Synopsis: A Jewish gangster in 1920s-1960s New York reflects on a lifetime of friendship betrayal and lost love in Leone's sprawling operatic epic.
Major_Awards: National Film Registry; considered Leone's magnum opus; Golden Globe nom; widely reassessed as a masterpiece

Title: Pink Floyd: The Wall
Synopsis: A burned-out rock star retreats behind a metaphorical wall built from childhood trauma, war loss, and adult disillusionment in this visually stunning blend of Roger Waters's music, Alan Parker's direction, and Gerald Scarfe's disturbing animation.

Title: Son of the White Mare
Synopsis: A cosmic white mare gives birth to three legendary sons who descend into the underworld to battle enormous dragons in this breathtaking Hungarian psychedelic animated epic rooted in ancient Magyar folklore.

Title: Terrorizers
Synopsis: A photographer's accidental snapshot of a delinquent girl sets off a chain of interconnected events that slowly destroys the lives of multiple Taipei residents in Edward Yang's chilling meditation on urban alienation and random violence.

Title: The Cook the Thief His Wife and Her Lover
Synopsis: A brutish gangster holds court at a gourmet restaurant while his wife conducts a secret affair with a bookish regular in this provocative allegory.
Major_Awards: Won BAFTA Special Award; controversial sensation; Peter Greenaway's most commercially successful and notorious film

Title: The Green Ray
Synopsis: A lonely young Parisian woman unable to find connection during her summer holiday drifts from resort to resort across France alone until a chance encounter at a seaside town offers the possibility of seeing the rare green flash of the setting sun.

Title: Threads
Synopsis: The nuclear bombing of Sheffield and its devastating twenty-year aftermath are depicted with documentary realism in this BBC film that remains the most harrowing portrayal of nuclear war ever committed to screen.

Title: Time of the Gypsies
Synopsis: A telekinetic young Romani man is recruited by a smooth-talking trafficker into a seedy criminal enterprise across Yugoslavia and Italy in Kusturica's sprawling magical-realist masterpiece about the corruption of innocence.

Title: Where Is the Friend's House?
Synopsis: A young Iranian boy must return his classmate's exercise book to prevent him being expelled in Kiarostami's deceptively simple and profoundly humane study of childhood conscience and adult indifference.

Title: Desert Hearts
Synopsis: A college professor awaiting her divorce in 1950s Reno begins a transformative romantic relationship with a free-spirited young woman.
Major_Awards: One of the first mainstream lesbian love stories; trailblazing LGBTQ cinema; Independent Spirit landmark
Key_Sources: Independent cinema landmark; LGBTQ film history

Title: The Dekalog
Synopsis: Ten one-hour films each inspired by one of the Ten Commandments explore the moral complexities of everyday life in a Warsaw housing estate.
Major_Awards: Venice Film Festival FIPRESCI; BFI Sight & Sound poll; widely considered one of the greatest achievements in the history of cinema
Key_Sources: BFI Sight & Sound; Venice Film Festival

Title: Batman
Synopsis: A brooding vigilante in a bat suit battles a psychotic criminal mastermind who has seized control of Gotham City's underworld.
Major_Awards: $251M domestic; cultural event of 1989; Jack Nicholson as the Joker; redefined superhero cinema; Tim Burton visual landmark

Title: A Question of Silence
Synopsis: Three Dutch women who have never met spontaneously kill a boutique manager together in this provocative feminist film that places systemic female rage on trial and asks whose silence the title actually refers to.

Title: A World Apart
Synopsis: A thirteen-year-old South African girl watches her anti-apartheid activist mother repeatedly detained under the Ninety-Day Act in this deeply personal drama based on the real autobiography of journalist Ruth First's daughter.

Title: Arthur
Synopsis: A lovable millionaire playboy must choose between marrying a wealthy heiress to keep his inheritance or following his heart to a working-class waitress.
Major_Awards: Won 2 Oscars (Supporting Actor John Gielgud, Original Song); $95M domestic; Dudley Moore charm offensive

Title: Berlin Alexanderplatz
Synopsis: A petty criminal released from prison in 1920s Weimar Berlin resolves to go straight but is slowly drawn back into violence and self-destruction in Fassbinder's epic fifteen-hour television adaptation of Alfred Döblin's modernist novel.

Title: Camille Claudel
Synopsis: The tumultuous career and tragic mental decline of gifted French sculptor Camille Claudel unfolds as her passionate and destructive relationship with Auguste Rodin and her emerging genius consume and ultimately overwhelm her.

Title: Camp de Thiaroye
Director: Ousmane Sembène and Thierno Faty Sow
Synopsis: African tirailleurs who fought for France in World War II demand their promised wages at a Senegalese transit camp and are massacred by French colonial forces in this devastating indictment of colonial betrayal and racial hypocrisy.

Title: Cocoon
Synopsis: Elderly residents of a retirement home discover that a mysterious swimming pool rejuvenates them after aliens leave energy pods in it.
Major_Awards: Won 2 Oscars (Supporting Actor Don Ameche, Visual Effects); $76M domestic

Title: I've Heard the Mermaids Singing
Synopsis: A dreamy and clumsy part-time secretary falls hopelessly in love with her cultured gallery-owner boss and secretly submits art as her own in this gentle and witty Canadian feminist comedy about art, fantasy, and self-deception.

Title: L'Ange
Synopsis: Human forms dissolve and metamorphose into one another in an endless dreamlike flux in this radically abstract French animated short by Patrick Bokanowski that operates entirely without narrative in a continuous state of visionary transformation.

Title: Mirch Masala
Synopsis: A rebellious woman refuses to submit to the sexual demands of a corrupt visiting tax collector and takes refuge in a spice mill where a group of women stand together to defend her in this acclaimed Indian feminist drama.

Title: My Beautiful Laundrette
Synopsis: A young British-Pakistani man transforms a rundown launderette into a thriving business with the help of his white working-class childhood friend and lover in this landmark of British cinema exploring race, class, and sexuality in Thatcher's England.

Title: My Brother's Wedding
Synopsis: A young Black man in South-Central Los Angeles is torn between loyalty to his street-tough friends and his upwardly mobile family as he navigates the painful contradictions of class and community in Charles Burnett's quiet devastation.

Title: Mystery Train
Synopsis: Three interconnected stories involving visitors to Memphis – two Japanese rock-and-roll pilgrims, a widowed Italian woman, and a British man mourning a breakup – converge overnight at a run-down hotel in this deadpan Jarmusch mood piece.

Title: Nostalghia
Synopsis: A Russian poet traveling through Italy becomes paralyzed by existential homesickness while forming a profound bond with a visionary local zealot in Tarkovsky's hypnotic meditation on displacement, faith, and the impossibility of return.

Title: Parting Glances
Synopsis: In the last twenty-four hours before his partner leaves for Africa a gay New Yorker navigates friends family and his former lover who is dying of AIDS in this warm and pioneering American film about gay urban life in the age of the epidemic.

Title: Pauline at the Beach
Synopsis: A worldly teenager and her romantically idealistic older cousin spend a summer by the sea encountering love, seduction, and the gap between theory and experience in this warm and witty entry in Rohmer's Comedies and Proverbs series.

Title: Polyester
Synopsis: A suburban Baltimore housewife with a cheating husband, a delinquent son, and terrible taste clings to romantic fantasies in John Waters's first mainstream comedy featuring Tab Hunter and Odorama scratch-and-sniff cards.

Title: Return of the Jedi
Synopsis: Luke Skywalker leads the mission to rescue Han Solo and then confronts Darth Vader and the Emperor as the Rebel Alliance attacks the new Death Star.
Major_Awards: Won Special Achievement Oscar; $309M domestic; National Film Registry; concluded the original Star Wars trilogy

Title: Rocky III
Synopsis: Rocky Balboa loses his title to a ferocious challenger and must regain his fighting spirit with the help of his former rival Apollo Creed.
Major_Awards: $125M domestic; Mr. T as Clubber Lang; Eye of the Tiger became iconic; reinvented the franchise

Title: Salaam Bombay!
Synopsis: A boy abandoned in Bombay survives and hustles on the city's streets while dreaming of earning enough to return home in Mira Nair's neorealist debut featuring powerful non-professional child performances.

Title: Smithereens
Synopsis: An ambitious young woman crashes her way into New York's punk underground through sheer audacity and manipulation but finds her schemes returning only loneliness in Susan Seidelman's raw and crackling debut feature.

Title: Sweet Bunch
Synopsis: A group of young middle-class Athenians drift through relationships, work, and political frustration in early 1980s Greece in Nikos Panayotopoulos's understated and quietly devastating portrait of a generation without direction.

Title: Taipei Story
Synopsis: A former baseball player clinging to the past and his restless girlfriend pulling toward the future struggle to maintain their relationship in this landmark of New Taiwanese Cinema and Edward Yang's breakthrough film.

Title: Taxi zum Klo
Synopsis: A gay West Berlin schoolteacher cruises public toilets and bathhouses while juggling a lover who wants something more conventional in this groundbreaking and joyfully explicit autobiographical portrait of gay sexual freedom in late 1970s Germany.

Title: The Ballad of Narayama
Synopsis: When a Japanese mountain villager turns seventy her dutiful son must carry her on his back up the sacred mountain to be left to die in the snow in Imamura's unsparing and magnificent examination of life, death, and filial duty.

Title: The Horse Thief
Synopsis: A Tibetan nomad expelled from his community for stealing from a monastery must survive with his family in the harsh landscape of this visually ravishing and spiritually profound film by Fifth Generation Chinese director Tian Zhuangzhuang.

Title: The Legend of Suram Fortress
Synopsis: An ancient Georgian legend about a young man walled alive inside a fortress to give it strength is told through Parajanov's hypnotic series of frozen tableaux saturated with folk imagery and rich color.

Title: Veronika Voss
Synopsis: A faded Ufa film star addicted to morphine dispensed by her sinister psychiatrist is investigated by a sports journalist obsessed with her in Fassbinder's luminous noir homage about postwar Germany's refusal to reckon honestly with its past.

Title: Diva
Synopsis: A young Parisian postman who secretly records an opera diva becomes entangled in two dangerous plots involving bootleg tapes and police corruption.
Major_Awards: 4 Cesar Awards; launched the Cinema du Look movement in France; style-defining film of 1980s French cinema

Title: Manon des Sources
Synopsis: Years after the events of Jean de Florette the dead man's beautiful daughter returns to exact an unknowing revenge on those who destroyed her father.
Major_Awards: Cesar Awards; massive international success; powerful companion piece completing one of cinema's great two-part stories

Title: Subway
Synopsis: A safe-cracker hides from gangsters in the Paris Metro and discovers an underground society of misfits musicians and dreamers.
Major_Awards: Cesar Awards for Best Actor/Director; Cinema du Look movement; Christophe Lambert/Isabelle Adjani; stylish 1980s French cinema

Title: The Big Blue
Synopsis: Two childhood friends become rival deep-sea divers competing for the world free-diving record in this visually stunning meditation on the call of the sea.
Major_Awards: Cesar Award for Best Sound/Music; massive international hit especially in France; Luc Besson's most personal film

Title: Grave of the Fireflies
Synopsis: Two Japanese siblings struggle to survive in the final months of World War II as firebombing and famine devastate their world.
Major_Awards: Considered one of the greatest animated and anti-war films ever made; Studio Ghibli masterpiece; Roger Ebert Great Movies
Key_Sources: BFI Sight & Sound; Roger Ebert Great Movies

Title: Labyrinth
Synopsis: A teenage girl must navigate a vast magical maze controlled by the Goblin King to rescue her baby brother before time runs out.
Major_Awards: David Bowie iconic performance; Jim Henson puppetry masterpiece; cult classic that grew in stature over decades

Title: Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind
Synopsis: A warrior princess tries to prevent two warring nations from destroying the toxic jungle that sustains Earth's fragile post-apocalyptic ecosystem.
Major_Awards: Animage Grand Prix; inspired the founding of Studio Ghibli; considered one of Miyazaki's finest works

Title: Raising Arizona
Synopsis: An ex-con and his police officer wife kidnap one of a wealthy couple's quintuplets in this hyperkinetic cartoon-like Coen Brothers comedy.
Major_Awards: Cult classic; established the Coens' visual and comedic style; widely regarded as one of the funniest films of the decade

Title: The Outsiders
Synopsis: Two rival teenage gangs from different sides of the tracks clash violently in 1960s Tulsa in this emotional adaptation of S.E. Hinton's novel.
Major_Awards: Launched careers of Tom Cruise Patrick Swayze Rob Lowe Matt Dillon Emilio Estevez; National Film Registry consideration

Title: The Shining
Synopsis: A writer takes a winter caretaker job at an isolated hotel where supernatural forces and his own madness threaten his wife and psychic young son.
Major_Awards: National Film Registry; BFI Sight & Sound poll; widely considered the greatest horror film ever made
Key_Sources: BFI Sight & Sound; National Film Registry

Title: Videodrome
Synopsis: A sleazy TV programmer discovers a broadcast signal that causes hallucinations and physical mutations blurring the line between media and flesh.
Major_Awards: Genie Award; prescient meditation on media consumption and technology; cult classic and Cronenberg masterpiece

Title: 84 Charing Cross Road
Synopsis: A spirited New York writer and a proper London antiquarian bookseller conduct a twenty-year correspondence that becomes a heartfelt trans-Atlantic literary friendship in this graceful adaptation of Helene Hanff's beloved memoir.

Title: A Chinese Ghost Story
Synopsis: A young tax collector sheltering in a haunted temple falls desperately in love with a female ghost enslaved by a tree demon and must fight to free her soul from the underworld in this ravishing Hong Kong supernatural romance.

Title: A Visitor to a Museum
Synopsis: A traveler makes a pilgrimage to a mysterious museum submerged under Soviet industrial water and encounters a community of mutants scraping survival from the ruins in this prophetic and visually astonishing Soviet science-fiction film.

Title: Akira
Synopsis: In a dystopian Neo-Tokyo a teenage biker gang member develops terrifying psychic powers that threaten to destroy the city in this landmark anime.
Major_Awards: Revolutionized anime in the West; widely regarded as one of the greatest animated films; influenced decades of sci-fi and cyberpunk

Title: Altered States
Synopsis: A scientist experimenting with sensory deprivation tanks and hallucinogenic drugs regresses to increasingly primitive states of consciousness in this Ken Russell spectacle that melds psychedelic experience with terrifying body horror.

Title: American Pop
Synopsis: Four generations of an immigrant Jewish family are woven through the entire history of American popular music from the turn of the century through the punk era in Ralph Bakshi's ambitious and visually inventive rotoscoped animated epic.

Title: Angel Heart
Synopsis: An NYC private detective is hired by a mysterious man named Louis Cyphre to track down a missing singer in the Deep South in this atmospheric supernatural noir with a genuinely shocking climax.

Title: Angel's Egg
Synopsis: In a devastated and enigmatic post-apocalyptic landscape a young girl wanders alone fiercely protecting a giant egg until a stranger arrives and challenges its meaning in this masterwork of Japanese experimental animation by Mamoru Oshii.

Title: Angst
Synopsis: A convicted killer is released from prison and immediately commits a terrifying home invasion against a family he encounters by chance in this relentlessly oppressive and formally daring Austrian psychological horror film.

Title: Anguish
Synopsis: A schizophrenic man under hypnotic control of his mother commits murders in a movie theater while inside a real theater the very film he is watching is causing someone else to commit murders in this breathtakingly self-referential Spanish horror.

Title: Barefoot Gen
Synopsis: The atomic bombing of Hiroshima in August 1945 is experienced through the eyes of six-year-old Gen whose family is obliterated in this harrowing and unflinching Japanese animated adaptation of Keiji Nakazawa's autobiographical manga.

Title: Bashu, the Little Stranger
Synopsis: A young boy from the south of Iran traumatized by the Iran-Iraq War flees north and is taken in by a resilient rural woman whose family and community resist his alien presence in this quietly powerful and humanistic Iranian film.

Title: Bianca
Synopsis: A high school teacher with a secret obsessive need to correct the immoral behavior of his neighbors becomes dangerously consumed by their lives in this dark and quietly disturbing Nanni Moretti portrait of bourgeois repression.

Title: Blood
Synopsis: Two brothers, Vicente and Nino, struggle to survive in a poverty-stricken Lisbon neighbourhood after their father's death, as their uncle tries to claim custody of Nino and debt collectors close in.

Title: Blood Wedding
Synopsis: Antonio Gades's flamenco company perform García Lorca's tragedy of forbidden love, blood feud, and fate in this spare and stunning filmed stage work that reduces the play to pure dance, music, and elemental emotion.

Title: Blue Mountains, or Unbelievable Story
Synopsis: The employees of a Soviet publishing house become so consumed with petty self-interest that they fail to notice the building literally crumbling around them in this brilliant Georgian satire of Soviet bureaucracy and collective indifference.

Title: Body Double
Synopsis: An unemployed actor housesitting a Hollywood mansion becomes obsessed with a neighbor he watches through a telescope and is drawn into a violent conspiracy in De Palma's gleefully provocative and self-aware Hitchcock homage.

Title: Born in Flames
Synopsis: Ten years after a peaceful American socialist revolution women of color and radicals organize guerrilla media networks and direct action to fight the persistent racism and sexism of the supposedly progressive new order.

Title: Breaker Morant
Synopsis: Three Australian officers are court-martialled for the execution of Boer prisoners during the Boer War in a military tribunal that functions as much as a political sacrifice to smooth colonial diplomacy as a genuine search for justice.

Title: Burden of Dreams
Synopsis: Les Blank documents the chaotic and nightmarish Amazon production of Herzog's Fitzcarraldo where the director's obsessive insistence on hauling a real steamship over a real mountain brings the production to the edge of total collapse.

Title: Castle in the Sky
Synopsis: A flying girl descends from the sky and a young miner must protect her from pirates and government agents as they search for a legendary floating island in this soaring and exhilaratingly inventive Miyazaki adventure.

Title: Casualties of War
Synopsis: A young American soldier is horrified when his sergeant orders the abduction and gang rape of a Vietnamese girl and must choose between loyalty to his unit and his own moral conscience in this searing De Palma Vietnam film.

Title: Celia
Synopsis: A nine-year-old Australian girl clings to her forbidden pet rabbit and retreats into increasingly dark fantasy as the Red Scare of 1952 destroys her family's community in this striking and deeply unsettling psychological debut by Ann Turner.

Title: Chan Is Missing
Synopsis: Two Chinese-American cab drivers in San Francisco search for their missing business partner through the neighborhoods of Chinatown in this landmark first feature directed by an Asian American and a founding text of Asian-American cinema.

Title: Christiane F.
Synopsis: A thirteen-year-old West Berlin girl descends into heroin addiction and prostitution around the drug scene of Zoo Station in this unflinching adaptation of a real teenager's account of surviving the Berlin underworld.

Title: City on Fire
Synopsis: An undercover Hong Kong cop infiltrates a gang of jewel thieves but forms a genuine bond with the thieves' leader in this propulsive crime film that served as a key visual and thematic source for Reservoir Dogs.

Title: Coal Miner's Daughter
Synopsis: The true story of country music legend Loretta Lynn traces her rise from hardscrabble poverty in rural Kentucky through her stormy marriage and her journey to become the queen of country music with a tour-de-force performance by Sissy Spacek.

Title: Damnation
Synopsis: A man obsessed with a married bar singer in a desolate Hungarian industrial town endlessly circling mud-soaked streets and rain-spattered bars becomes the foundation for Béla Tarr's signature long-take monochrome style.

Title: Day of the Dead
Synopsis: A small group of soldiers and scientists shelter in an underground bunker as a zombie apocalypse rages above and the conflict between military brutality and scientific experimentation on the undead drives the survivors toward catastrophe.

Title: Dead Man's Letters
Synopsis: After a nuclear war a man lives in the ruins of a museum and writes letters to his dead son while caring for radiation victims gathering around him in this poetic and devastating Soviet post-apocalyptic film by Konstantin Lopushansky.

Title: Dead Ringers
Synopsis: Identical twin gynecologists become dangerously indistinguishable to their patients and eventually themselves as one descends into drug addiction and slowly drags his brother into oblivion in Cronenberg's most disturbing meditation on identity and bodily horror.

Title: Death of Yazdgerd
Synopsis: On the night of the murder of the last Sassanid Persian king a miller's family is accused of sheltering the emperor and subjected to brutal interrogation in this dense Brechtian Iranian film by Bahram Beizai.

Title: Down by Law
Synopsis: Three misfits thrown together in a New Orleans jail break out and wander through the Louisiana bayou in this deadpan existential comedy.
Major_Awards: One of the defining American independent films of the 1980s; Jim Jarmusch landmark; Tom Waits and Roberto Benigni star

Title: Dressed to Kill
Synopsis: A sexually frustrated housewife is murdered in an elevator and the killer then targets the call girl who witnessed the killing in De Palma's relentlessly stylish Hitchcock homage that divided critics with its ferocious provocation.

Title: Duel to the Death
Synopsis: The greatest swordsmen of China and Japan meet for a legendary duel that becomes entangled with espionage, ninja assassins, and supernatural forces in this extraordinary and inventive wuxia spectacular.

Title: Eastern Condors
Synopsis: A group of Vietnamese-American criminals are recruited on a suicide mission to destroy a secret ammunition dump in post-war Vietnam in this spectacularly choreographed Hong Kong action film by Sammo Hung.

Title: El amor brujo
Synopsis: Spain's finest flamenco company perform Carlos Saura's cinematic staging of Manuel de Falla's ballet about a young gypsy woman haunted by the possessive ghost of her murdered first husband in this third in Saura's acclaimed flamenco trilogy.

Title: El Keif
Synopsis: An Egyptian chemist creates a harmless hashish substitute to wean his addicted brother off drugs, but the cunning scheme is hijacked by criminal drug traffickers, drawing both brothers into a dangerous spiral of deception and crime.

Title: El Sur
Synopsis: A young girl in Franco's Spain idolizes her enigmatic father and slowly senses the hidden sadness of the southern life he has permanently left behind in Victor Erice's achingly beautiful and incomplete fragment about memory and paternal mystery.

Title: Elvira: Mistress of the Dark
Synopsis: TV horror hostess Elvira inherits a creepy mansion in the conservative New England town of Fallwell Massachusetts in this gleefully campy comedy that revels in double entendres, monster suits, and cheerful bad taste.

Title: Encounters of the Spooky Kind
Synopsis: A foolhardy man is manipulated into spending the night in a haunted house by his cuckolding wife and her lover leading to frantic encounters with black magic and hopping vampires in this seminal Sammo Hung blend of horror and slapstick comedy.

Title: Escape from New York
Synopsis: In a dystopian future Manhattan is a maximum-security prison and a lone anti-hero must rescue the President who has crash-landed inside.
Major_Awards: Cult classic; $25M domestic on $6M budget; Kurt Russell as Snake Plissken became iconic; John Carpenter landmark

Title: For All Mankind
Synopsis: NASA's Apollo lunar mission footage is assembled with astronaut oral histories and Brian Eno's haunting score into the definitive cinematic record of humanity's most extraordinary collective achievement.

Title: Garlic Is as Good as Ten Mothers
Synopsis: Les Blank surveys the glorious world of garlic culture through California's annual Gilroy Garlic Festival in this exuberant short documentary celebrating the pleasures of cooking and the stinking rose.

Title: Golden Eighties
Synopsis: The employees and customers of a Brussels shopping arcade sing, flirt, and scheme in this stylized and witty Chantal Akerman musical comedy that transforms the consumer spaces of the 1980s into surprisingly tender spectacle.

Title: Good Morning, Vietnam
Synopsis: An irreverent and anarchic DJ assigned to Armed Forces Radio in 1965 Saigon becomes a sensation among the troops while the escalating reality of the Vietnam War slowly seeps into his life and performances.

Title: Hachiko
Synopsis: The true story of the loyal Akita dog who returned to Shibuya station every evening to wait for his beloved owner for nearly a decade after the man's sudden death in this moving Japanese biographical film.

Title: Heart of a Dog
Synopsis: A Moscow professor's surgical implant of a dead man's glands into a stray dog produces a crude and politically connected human being in Vladimir Bortko's sharp and acclaimed Soviet TV adaptation of Bulgakov's banned satirical novella.

Title: Heaven's Gate
Synopsis: A class war erupts in 1890s Wyoming between established cattle barons and newly arrived immigrant settlers as an idealistic Harvard graduate watches the country he believed in devour itself in this epic and misconceived revisionist Western.

Title: Henry V
Synopsis: Shakespeare's warrior king leads a battered English army to a decisive victory against overwhelming odds at Agincourt in Kenneth Branagh's triumphant directorial debut that reinvented Shakespeare for a generation raised on cinema.

Title: Homework
Synopsis: Kiarostami films intimate conversations with elementary school boys about their homework habits revealing with touching humanity and startling statistical precision the difficulty of studying in crowded Iranian households.

Title: In a Glass Cage
Synopsis: A former Nazi doctor paralyzed after a failed suicide is kept alive in an iron lung until a young man claiming to be one of his victims arrives and begins methodically reenacting the doctor's crimes in this extremely disturbing Spanish horror.

Title: Jaane Bhi Do Yaaro
Synopsis: Two struggling photographers accidentally film a corrupt murder and find themselves enmeshed in a conspiracy of venal politicians and crooked property developers in this beloved Indian black comedy widely considered the greatest Indian satire ever made.

Title: Jane B. by Agnès V.
Synopsis: Agnès Varda's playful and probing portrait of actress Jane Birkin allows Birkin to reinvent herself through elaborate fantasy scenarios while serving as a witty meditation on femininity, moviemaking, and the nature of female friendship.

Title: Kagero-za
Synopsis: A Taisho-era playwright is drawn into an erotic obsession with a patron's mysterious wife and a story that refuses to distinguish between theater, dream, and reality in Seijun Suzuki's gorgeously surreal oneiric masterpiece.

Title: Kin-dza-dza!
Synopsis: Two Soviet men accidentally teleported to a dying desert planet discover that survival depends on bells and trouser color in this beloved Soviet science-fiction comedy about power, degradation, and the resilience of human dignity.

Title: Kireedam
Synopsis: A police officer struggles with guilt and moral burden after his reformed father is sent to prison through a miscarriage of justice in this acclaimed and emotionally devastating Malayalam drama by Sibi Malayil.

Title: Kisapmata
Synopsis: A tyrannical Filipino patriarch controls every aspect of his daughter's life with terrifying possessive obsession even after her marriage in this suffocating domestic horror film considered one of the greatest Philippine films ever made.

Title: L'Argent
Synopsis: A forged banknote passed among characters gradually destroys the life of an innocent delivery man who is imprisoned and emerges transformed into terrible violence in Bresson's final film and one of cinema's most severe and formally perfect works.

Title: La Bamba
Synopsis: The brief meteoric life of Ritchie Valens the young Mexican-American rock-and-roll pioneer who died aged seventeen in the same 1959 plane crash that killed Buddy Holly is told with warmth, music, and family feeling.

Title: Landscape Suicide
Synopsis: Experimental filmmaker James Benning intercuts two long-form reenactments of murder confessions from Bernadette Protti and an account drawn from Ed Gein's crimes with static images of American landscape in this radically stripped-down documentary.

Title: Le Pont du Nord
Synopsis: Two women form an uneasy friendship and traverse Paris following a map carved on the city's fountains in what seems to be a real or imaginary game in Jacques Rivette's enigmatic and playful final film of his 1970s cycle.

Title: Leila and the Wolves
Synopsis: A woman travels through time witnessing and joining Palestinian and Lebanese women's resistance against colonial occupation and civil war in this remarkable experimental documentary-fiction hybrid of deep political passion.

Title: Let's Get Lost
Synopsis: Bruce Weber's black-and-white portrait of jazz trumpeter Chet Baker intercuts images of his charismatic youth with footage of his ravaged later years creating a film as much about myth, beauty, and self-destruction as about music.

Title: Lion of the Desert
Synopsis: Libyan guerrilla leader Omar Mukhtar wages a decades-long resistance against Mussolini's brutal Italian occupation of Libya in this epic historical drama with Anthony Quinn delivering a towering and dignity-filled performance.

Title: Macross: Do You Remember Love?
Synopsis: Humans, giants, and female alien warriors battle for survival in outer space while a love triangle among three key figures determines the fate of three civilizations in this theatrical retelling that elevated the Macross franchise to landmark status.

Title: Mad Max 2
Synopsis: A laconic lone drifter reluctantly helps a community of petrol-producing survivors defend themselves against a brutal motorcycle gang in this extraordinarily visceral and seminal Australian action film that redefined post-apocalyptic cinema.

Title: Man Facing Southeast
Synopsis: A psychiatrist at a Buenos Aires hospital is increasingly disturbed by a patient who calmly claims to be an alien observer sent to study humanity and whose increasingly difficult-to-dismiss claims draw the doctor to dangerous sympathies.

Title: Matewan
Synopsis: A labor organizer arrives in a West Virginia mining town in 1920 to help Black, white, and Italian immigrant miners unite against the Stone Mountain Coal Company in a story of solidarity, betrayal, and violence based on actual events.

Title: Mauvais Sang
Synopsis: Three people plan an audacious heist involving a rare virus-laden serum in this visually intoxicating Leos Carax film stitching together film noir, Godard homage, Denis Lavant's explosive dancing, and aching adolescent longing.

Title: Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence
Synopsis: The complex and suppressed relationship between a British prisoner of war and his Japanese commandant in a World War II prison camp becomes a meditation on honor, repressed desire, and the clash of Eastern and Western codes of masculinity.

Title: Midnight Run
Synopsis: A by-the-book bail bondsman must transport a mob accountant cross-country by bus, train, and foot while evading the FBI, rival bounty hunters, and the mob itself in this supremely crafted buddy comedy with Robert De Niro and Charles Grodin.

Title: Miracle Mile
Synopsis: A man answers a ringing payphone at 4am and hears a panicked soldier warning that a nuclear strike will hit Los Angeles in seventy minutes and must decide whether the call is real while desperately searching for the woman he just met.

Title: Mobile Suit Gundam: Char's Counterattack
Synopsis: The final confrontation between rival pilots Amuro Ray and Char Aznable climaxes as Char attempts to drop an asteroid on Earth to force humanity to evolve in this operatic conclusion to the original Gundam saga.

Title: Monty Python's The Meaning of Life
Synopsis: The Monty Python team examines the major stages of human existence from birth through death and beyond in a series of increasingly blasphemous, grotesque, and brilliantly designed sketches culminating in the Mr. Creosote sequence.

Title: Moral
Synopsis: Four young Filipino women navigate marriage, abortion, marital rape, sexuality, and political activism across several years after graduating university in this landmark feminist drama set in the Martial Law-era Philippines.

Title: Mr. Vampire
Synopsis: A Taoist priest and his bumbling apprentices must handle the corpse of a newly dead man that threatens to become a jiangshi hopping vampire in this milestone Hong Kong horror comedy that founded and defined an entire subgenre.

Title: Mur Murs
Synopsis: Agnès Varda documents Los Angeles's extraordinary mural tradition as a window into the city's diverse communities in this rich and playful documentary exploring the relationship between public art and lived experience in California.

Title: My Dinner with Andre
Synopsis: Two friends share a long dinner conversation that ranges from profound philosophical reflections to deeply personal confessions about life and art.
Major_Awards: One of the most influential conversational films ever made; widely parodied and referenced; Independent cinema landmark

Title: Nayakan
Synopsis: Loosely based on real Mumbai crime boss Varadarajan Mudaliar this Tamil epic follows a man who flees to Bombay after killing his father's murderer and rises to become a beloved crime lord and community protector in Mani Ratnam's magisterial film.

Title: Neo Tokyo
Director: Rintaro and Yoshiaki Kawajiri and Katsuhiro Otomo
Synopsis: Three avant-garde animators – Rintaro, Yoshiaki Kawajiri, and Katsuhiro Otomo – each contribute a visually explosive short to this anthology exploring racing with death, corrupt mechanical circuses, and a youth with terrifying powers.

Title: Night on the Galactic Railroad
Synopsis: A lonely Japanese boy boards a mysterious train that carries him across an animated galaxy of stars and constellations discovering the meaning of life, friendship, and death in this beautiful and melancholy adaptation of Kenji Miyazawa's beloved novel.

Title: Nostos: The Return
Synopsis: A traveler returns to a landscape of ruined villas and misty northern Italian waterways in this Odyssey-inspired film by Franco Piavoli that works almost without dialogue through pure elemental imagery and the rhythm of nature.

Title: O-Bi, O-Ba: The End of Civilization
Synopsis: Survivors of nuclear war huddle underground waiting for an ark promised to ferry them to safety which may exist only as a collective myth necessary for survival in this devastating Polish post-apocalyptic parable by Piotr Szulkin.

Title: On the Silver Globe
Synopsis: Cosmonauts crashing on a distant planet found a new civilization whose descendants face the religious structures their ancestors created in Andrzej Zulawski's extraordinary unfinished science-fiction epic released with narrated bridges for missing footage.

Title: Opera
Synopsis: A young soprano performing Macbeth receives anonymous love letters from a maniac who forces her to watch while he murders people close to her in Argento's most technically dazzling combination of giallo violence and operatic grandeur.

Title: Patlabor: The Movie
Synopsis: Tokyo police detectives investigate mysterious suicides connected to a major software project while piloted labor robots are used citywide for infrastructure work in this thoughtful and elegantly paced science-fiction mystery by Mamoru Oshii.

Title: Peking Opera Blues
Synopsis: Three women from wildly different backgrounds form an unlikely alliance during the chaotic warlord period of 1913 China in this dazzling Tsui Hark blend of physical comedy, political intrigue, and bittersweet romantic feeling.

Title: Phenomena
Synopsis: A young girl with the ability to communicate telepathically with insects investigates a series of brutal murders near her Swiss boarding school with the help of an entomologist and his chimpanzee in this exuberant Argento spectacle.

Title: Poison for the Fairies
Synopsis: Two little girls form an intense friendship but one is obsessed with witchcraft and masterfully manipulates the other into taking increasingly dark and dangerous steps in this eerie and distinctive Mexican psychological horror film.

Title: Police Story
Synopsis: A Hong Kong supercop protecting a drug lord's secretary escalates through a spectacular series of physical set-pieces as his personal life collapses and the film ends with one of cinema's most extraordinary shopping mall showdowns.

Title: Possession
Synopsis: A couple's marriage catastrophically disintegrates in a divided Berlin as the husband discovers his wife is conducting a monstrous affair with something inhuman in Andrzej Zulawski's operatic horror about the annihilating violence of love's end.

Title: Prince: Sign 'o' the Times
Synopsis: Prince performs songs from his landmark double album in this concert film integrated with short dramatic sequences featuring Sheena Easton and Sheila E in a definitive document of the artist at the absolute peak of his creative powers.

Title: Roots
Synopsis: A young Georgian peasant who emigrated to Paris in 1917 builds a life in France but never loses his love for his homeland, a longing he passes on to his grandson, who ultimately fulfils his grandfather's dying wish to have his ashes returned to Georgia.

Title: Rouge
Synopsis: A legendary courtesan from 1930s Hong Kong appears as a ghost in the present day searching for the lover with whom she made a suicide pact in Stanley Kwan's ravishing supernatural romance about memory, fidelity, and the passage of time.

Title: Royal Space Force - The Wings of Honneamise
Synopsis: An aimless young man in an alternate world's struggling space program decides to become his civilization's first astronaut in this astonishingly ambitious Gainax debut feature that builds an entire alternate world in service of a profoundly humanistic story.

Title: Running on Empty
Synopsis: Two teenage sons of radical fugitives living permanently on the run from the FBI must choose between the life their parents have given them and a future of their own in this Sidney Lumet drama featuring River Phoenix's most widely celebrated performance.

Title: Santa Sangre
Synopsis: A young circus performer escapes from a mental asylum and rejoins his armless cult-leader mother who uses his arms as her own to commit murders in Alejandro Jodorowsky's most visually overwhelming and psychologically layered surrealist masterwork.

Title: Sherman's March
Synopsis: Documentary filmmaker Ross McElwee sets out to trace Sherman's Civil War march through the South but becomes instead an obsessive self-portrait of himself endlessly failing at love while encountering a gallery of remarkable Southern women.

Title: Space Runaway Ideon: Be Invoked
Synopsis: The crew of the alien mecha Ideon faces total annihilation in Yoshiyuki Tomino's apocalyptic theatrical finale to his most despairing science-fiction series, ending with the literal extinction of all human and alien life.

Title: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
Synopsis: Kirk and crew travel back in time to 1980s San Francisco to bring two humpback whales to the 23rd century to answer an alien probe threatening Earth in the most beloved and crowd-pleasing of all the Star Trek feature films.

Title: Streetwise
Synopsis: A group of homeless teenagers hustling, panhandling, and surviving on the streets of Seattle give raw and compassionate testimony in this extraordinary vérité documentary about children utterly abandoned by American society.

Title: Style Wars
Synopsis: New York subway graffiti writers compete for fame and develop their art while the transit authority wages war to eradicate their work in this definitive documentary record of the visual culture that launched from hip-hop's earliest years.

Title: Tangos, the Exile of Gardel
Synopsis: Argentine political exiles in Paris attempt to stage a tango show about their displacement while grieving for their lost country and mourning the spirit of Carlos Gardel in Fernando Solanas's bittersweet elegy on cultural exile.

Title: Tenebre
Synopsis: A successful American crime novelist visiting Rome discovers that his newest book is inspiring a real serial killer who targets people connected to the author in this supremely crafted Argento film that deconstructs its own giallo genre.

Title: Tetsuo: The Iron Man
Synopsis: A Japanese businessman begins transforming into a hybrid of flesh and metal in this intensely energetic black-and-white Japanese cyberpunk horror film shot in a relentless industrial assault style by Shinya Tsukamoto.

Title: The 4th Man
Synopsis: A bisexual Dutch writer becomes dangerously obsessed with a seductive widow and suspects she may have murdered her previous three husbands in this visually extravagant Paul Verhoeven erotic thriller shot through with Catholic guilt and dark humor.

Title: The 8 Diagram Pole Fighter
Synopsis: Five sons of a betrayed general are massacred in a Mongol ambush and the surviving son joins a Buddhist monastery where he perfects the pole fighting style needed to eventually avenge his family's annihilation in this classic Shaw Brothers epic.

Title: The Big Red One
Synopsis: A hardened World War II sergeant leads his four-man squad of infantrymen from North Africa through Sicily, France, Belgium, and Czechoslovakia in Samuel Fuller's deeply personal and autobiographical account of war at ground level.

Title: The Blob
Synopsis: A gelatinous alien organism arrives in a small California town and begins dissolving every human being it touches while a rebellious young woman and a motorcycle-riding outsider try desperately to stop its spread in this energetic and gory remake.

Title: The Boxer's Omen
Synopsis: A Hong Kong man travels to Thailand after his champion boxer brother is paralyzed and finds himself entangled with black magic monks and demonic priests in this spectacularly grotesque Shaw Brothers supernatural horror film.

Title: The Dark Crystal
Synopsis: A young Gelfling embarks on a quest to restore a powerful crystal and heal his world in this ambitious all-puppet dark fantasy.
Major_Awards: Jim Henson's most ambitious puppet film; Saturn Award nom; cult classic; groundbreaking creature design

Title: The Emperor's Naked Army Marches On
Synopsis: An obsessive aging veteran confronts his former commanding officers one by one demanding they account for the death and alleged cannibalism of his unit comrades in wartime New Guinea in this remarkable and deeply unsettling Japanese confrontational documentary.

Title: The Fox and the Hound
Director: Art Stevens and Ted Berman and Richard Rich
Synopsis: A fox and a hound form a childhood friendship that is tested as they grow into their natural roles as predator and prey in this underrated Disney feature marking the transition from the old animators' guard to the generation that would create the Renaissance.

Title: The Great Muppet Caper
Synopsis: Kermit and Fozzie travel to London as journalist brothers to cover a jewel theft and get entangled with Miss Piggy's fashion world ambitions and a daring heist in this inventive and self-aware second Muppet theatrical feature directed by Jim Henson.

Title: The Hidden
Synopsis: A reserved police detective works with an FBI agent unfamiliar with human customs to track a parasitic alien creature that inhabits human bodies and compulsively steals fast cars and commits spectacular violence in this sharply genre-subverting thriller.

Title: The Hitcher
Synopsis: A young man driving cross-country picks up a hitchhiker who reveals himself as a psychopathic killer and then systematically destroys the young man's life across empty desert highways in this lean and relentlessly tense road horror.

Title: The King and the Mockingbird
Synopsis: An evil king is challenged by a mockingbird defending a shepherd and chimney sweep in Paul Grimault's French animated masterwork thirty years in the making and widely considered the greatest European animated feature film.

Title: The Last Metro
Synopsis: During the Nazi occupation of Paris a theater director hides a Jewish Jewish director in the building's cellar while his wife manages the company and falls for a magnetic new leading actor in Truffaut's most commercially successful and warmly embraced film.

Title: The Last Unicorn
Director: Jules Bass and Arthur Rankin Jr.
Synopsis: The last unicorn sets out to find what became of others of her kind and discovers the evil Red Bull has driven them all into the sea at the castle of the wretched King Haggard in this melancholy and exquisitely animated Rankin-Bass fantasy.

Title: The Legend of the Stardust Brothers
Synopsis: Two rival aspiring pop singers are discovered by a slick record producer and rocket to fame only to be separated and exploited by the industry in this wildly colorful Japanese rock musical that became a beloved cult legend.

Title: The Lost Boys
Synopsis: Two brothers move to a California beach town secretly populated by a gang of beautiful teenage vampires in this supremely cool and atmospheric blend of teen movie, horror, and 1980s style from Joel Schumacher.

Title: The Pied Piper
Synopsis: The medieval legend of the Pied Piper of Hamelin is reimagined through Jiří Barta's extraordinary puppet animation style as an allegory of political manipulation, collective self-interest, and the disregard of promises made to the powerless.

Title: The Plague Dogs
Synopsis: Two escaped laboratory dogs become fugitives hunted across the English Lake District by soldiers who fear they may carry a deadly disease in this brutal and unsparing animated adaptation of Richard Adams's devastatingly anti-vivisection novel.

Title: The Return of the Living Dead
Synopsis: Bumbling workers accidentally release a military chemical that reanimates the dead in this gleefully anarchic punk horror comedy that gave the world flesh-eating zombies specifically craving human brains and pioneered the genre's dark comic potential.

Title: The Secret of NIMH
Synopsis: A widowed field mouse must move her family before the farmer's plow destroys their home and seeks help from a mysterious colony of intellectually enhanced rats in Don Bluth's first theatrical feature and a genuinely great animated film.

Title: The Secret of the Third Planet
Synopsis: A young girl and a spaceship captain's son rescue a rare alien animal smuggled from a distant planet in this charming and inventive Soviet animated space opera full of original creature designs and comic invention.

Title: The Seventh Curse
Synopsis: A Hong Kong doctor battles ancient blood curses, tribal warlords, and a skeleton demon in Thailand in this outrageous and breathlessly entertaining Hong Kong pulp horror adventure that packs more insanity per frame than almost any comparable film.

Title: The Thin Blue Line
Synopsis: A groundbreaking documentary reexamines the case of a man convicted of murdering a Dallas police officer and ultimately helps overturn his conviction.
Major_Awards: National Film Registry; NY Film Critics Best Documentary; revolutionized documentary filmmaking; freed an innocent man
Key_Sources: National Film Registry; NY Film Critics

Title: The Times of Harvey Milk
Synopsis: This Academy Award-winning documentary chronicles Harvey Milk's rise as San Francisco's first openly gay supervisor and the devastating impact of his 1978 assassination on the city's LGBTQ community and American political life.

Title: The War of the Worlds: Next Century
Synopsis: A television journalist becomes willing propagandist for an alien invasion of his country in this Polish science-fiction drama by Piotr Szulkin that uses the invasion metaphor to analyze media complicity in totalitarian domination.

Title: They Live
Synopsis: A drifter discovers sunglasses that reveal aliens have taken over Earth and control humanity through subliminal messages in media and advertising.
Major_Awards: Cult classic; prophetic anti-consumerist satire; iconic put on the glasses and fight scenes

Title: Time for Revenge
Synopsis: An industrial worker fakes his own deafness after surviving an accident caused by corporate negligence and meticulously plans an elaborate scheme to destroy the company responsible in this gripping and intelligent Argentine thriller.

Title: Time Masters
Synopsis: A boy stranded on a planet inhabited by murderous hornets communicates by radio with a group racing across space to reach him in René Laloux's visually stunning animated science-fiction film with designs by the legendary comic artist Moebius.

Title: To Live and Die in L.A.
Synopsis: Two Secret Service agents hunt a ruthless counterfeiter through the neon-lit underworld of 1980s Los Angeles in this supremely stylish and morally nihilistic crime film featuring one of cinema's most spectacular and genuinely dangerous car chases.

Title: Tongues Untied
Synopsis: Marlon Riggs's poetic documentary combines personal testimony, performance, and spoken word poetry to assert the complexity and beauty of Black gay male identity in the heart of the Reagan-era AIDS crisis.

Title: Top Secret!
Director: Jim Abrahams and David Zucker and Jerry Zucker
Synopsis: An American rock star visits East Germany for a cultural exchange and gets entangled with the French Resistance, a beautiful woman, and an increasingly absurd series of misadventures in this wall-to-wall visual gag machine from the ZAZ team.

Title: True Stories
Synopsis: David Byrne drives through the fictional Texas town of Virgil on the occasion of its sesquicentennial and visits its remarkable residents in this deadpan and affectionate portrait of American eccentricity set to Talking Heads music.

Title: Twenty Years Later
Synopsis: Eduardo Coutinho returns after two decades to find and photograph a northeastern Brazilian peasant he had previously documented and discovers the man was murdered by landowners after the original film brought attention to his resistance.

Title: Urusei Yatsura: Beautiful Dreamer
Synopsis: The students of Tomobiki High School find themselves trapped in an endless loop the night before a school festival as time itself begins to fracture in this Mamoru Oshii film that transformed a slapstick comedy franchise into contemplative science fiction.

Title: Utopia
Synopsis: A bleak West German portrait of a pimp and his five girls living on the margins of society, directed by Iranian-born filmmaker Sohrab Shahid-Saless and entered into the 33rd Berlin International Film Festival.

Title: Victor/Victoria
Synopsis: A starving soprano in 1930s Paris masquerades as a man posing as a female impersonator and becomes a sensation until a Chicago gangster falls for her and must decide what his attraction means in this witty gender comedy by Blake Edwards.

Title: Walker
Synopsis: The 1850s mercenary William Walker's self-proclaimed presidency of Nicaragua is told with deliberate anachronism and savage black comedy by Alex Cox in this brilliant and bracingly angry critique of American interventionism in Latin America.

Title: When the Wind Blows
Synopsis: An elderly English couple cheerfully follow government nuclear war survival advice as they slowly die of radiation poisoning in this devastatingly gentle animated film that exposes the lethal absurdity of official nuclear preparedness.

Title: White Dog
Synopsis: A young actress takes in a stray white dog only to discover he has been conditioned to attack Black people on sight in this brave and troubling Samuel Fuller film about racism and whether racist violence can ever truly be unlearned.

Title: Who's Singin' Over There?
Synopsis: Passengers on a decrepit bus journey through wartime Yugoslavia encounter increasingly strange characters while the driver's two sons sing folk songs in this darkly comic Slobodan Šijan ensemble piece leading to an unforgettable final revelation.

Title: Zigeunerweisen
Synopsis: A university professor encounters a mysterious drifter whose connection to a haunting violin recording gradually collapses the boundaries between the living and the dead in Seijun Suzuki's dreamlike first entry in his Taisho Roman Trilogy.

Title: 48 Hrs.
Synopsis: A no-nonsense cop reluctantly teams up with a fast-talking convict to track down a pair of cop killers in 48 hours.
Major_Awards: $78M domestic; created the buddy-cop genre; Eddie Murphy film debut; launched a template copied for decades

Title: A Better Tomorrow
Synopsis: Two brothers on opposite sides of the law are tested when the elder is imprisoned and his flamboyant criminal partner played by Chow Yun-fat seeks brutal revenge in this genre-defining Hong Kong action film.
Major_Awards: Created the heroic bloodshed genre; Chow Yun-fat became an international icon; Hong Kong Film Awards Best Picture and Best Actor; enormous influence on world action cinema including Tarantino and Woo's own Hollywood career

Title: A Christmas Story
Synopsis: In 1940s Indiana a bespectacled boy desperately schemes to get a Red Ryder BB gun for Christmas while navigating bullies and family chaos.
Major_Awards: National Film Registry; became the most beloved American Christmas film through annual TV marathons

Title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
Synopsis: Teenagers are stalked in their dreams by a horribly burned killer with razor-blade fingers who can kill them in their sleep.
Major_Awards: $25M domestic on $1.8M budget; launched Freddy Krueger as horror icon; National Film Registry; Wes Craven career-defining
Key_Sources: National Film Registry; Box Office Mojo

Title: Airplane!
Director: Jim Abrahams and David Zucker and Jerry Zucker
Synopsis: A traumatized former fighter pilot must land a commercial aircraft after the crew is incapacitated in this relentlessly hilarious disaster movie parody.
Major_Awards: AFI Top 100 Laughs (#10); $83M domestic on $3.5M budget; revolutionized spoof comedy; National Film Registry

Title: An American Tail
Synopsis: A young Russian mouse emigrates to America in the 1880s and is separated from his family while searching for a land with no cats.
Major_Awards: $47M domestic; Spielberg produced; Don Bluth's biggest hit; Somewhere Out There became a hit song; outgrossed Disney's release that year

Title: Back to the Future Part II
Synopsis: Marty McFly travels to 2015 to prevent his son's arrest but inadvertently creates an alternate dystopian timeline he must race to correct.
Major_Awards: $118M domestic; ambitious time-travel sequel; iconic hoverboard and self-lacing sneakers became cultural predictions

Title: Bill and Ted's Excellent Adventure
Synopsis: Two dopey teenage metalheads travel through time collecting historical figures for their high school history presentation to avoid flunking out.
Major_Awards: $40M domestic; cult classic; Keanu Reeves breakout; iconic Excellent catchphrase; beloved 1980s comedy

Title: Blow Out
Synopsis: A movie sound effects technician accidentally records audio evidence of a political assassination and becomes a target himself.
Major_Awards: Brian De Palma's finest thriller; John Travolta's best dramatic performance; deeply Hitchcockian; National Film Registry

Title: Caddyshack
Synopsis: Class warfare erupts at an exclusive golf club when a boorish new member clashes with the uptight establishment while a deranged groundskeeper battles a gopher.
Major_Awards: AFI Top 100 Laughs; $39M domestic; one of the most quoted comedies of all time; launched Chevy Chase Bill Murray careers

Title: Clan of the Cave Bear
Synopsis: A Cro-Magnon girl is adopted by a Neanderthal clan and struggles to fit in while her advanced abilities threaten the tribe's traditions.
Major_Awards: Controversial adaptation of Jean Auel's novel; Daryl Hannah; ambitious prehistoric drama

Title: Clue
Synopsis: Six strangers are invited to a gothic mansion for a dinner party where murder ensues and everyone is a suspect in this farce with multiple endings.
Major_Awards: Initially underperformed; became one of the most beloved cult comedies through home video; adapted from the board game

Title: Come and See
Synopsis: A Belarusian teenager's harrowing journey through Nazi-occupied countryside becomes a visceral descent into the absolute horror of total war.
Major_Awards: BFI Sight & Sound poll; FIPRESCI Prize Moscow; widely considered the greatest war film ever made
Key_Sources: BFI Sight & Sound; Moscow Film Festival

Title: Conan the Barbarian
Synopsis: A young warrior enslaved as a child grows to become a mighty barbarian who seeks revenge against the sorcerer who destroyed his people.
Major_Awards: $39M domestic; Arnold Schwarzenegger breakthrough; Basil Poledouris iconic score; redefined sword-and-sorcery cinema

Title: Evil Dead II
Synopsis: Ash Williams returns to the cabin in the woods for a manic slapstick horror sequel that brilliantly blends Three Stooges comedy with demonic mayhem.
Major_Awards: Cult classic; widely considered superior to the original; defined horror-comedy genre for decades to come

Title: Fast Times at Ridgemont High
Synopsis: A group of Southern California teenagers navigate high school romance employment and growing up in this candid ensemble comedy.
Major_Awards: National Film Registry; launched careers of Sean Penn Jennifer Jason Leigh Judge Reinhold; defined 1980s teen comedy

Title: Ferris Buellers Day Off
Synopsis: A charming high school senior fakes illness to skip school and takes his best friend and girlfriend on an unforgettable day across Chicago.
Major_Awards: National Film Registry; $70M domestic; one of the most celebrated comedies of the decade
Key_Sources: National Film Registry; Box Office Mojo

Title: First Blood
Synopsis: A traumatized Vietnam veteran is harassed by a small-town sheriff and unleashes his combat skills in a one-man war against local authorities.
Major_Awards: $47M domestic; launched the Rambo franchise; surprisingly nuanced portrayal of PTSD for its era

Title: Gallipoli
Synopsis: Two young Australian sprinters enlist to fight in World War I and face the devastating futility of the Gallipoli campaign.
Major_Awards: Australian Film Institute Best Film/Director; Peter Weir's international breakthrough; devastating anti-war vision

Title: Gremlins
Synopsis: A teenage boy receives an unusual pet that spawns small destructive monsters who terrorize a small town on Christmas Eve.
Major_Awards: $148M domestic; led to creation of PG-13 rating; Spielberg-produced; perfect blend of comedy and horror

Title: Honey I Shrunk the Kids
Synopsis: An inventor accidentally shrinks his children and the neighbors' kids to quarter-inch height and they must traverse the now-deadly backyard.
Major_Awards: $130M domestic; $222M worldwide; Rick Moranis; launched Disney's live-action family franchise

Title: Koyaanisqatsi
Synopsis: A wordless visual poem juxtaposes images of nature and modern civilization set to Philip Glass's hypnotic minimalist score.
Major_Awards: National Film Registry; one of the most influential experimental films; redefined non-narrative cinema

Title: Lethal Weapon
Synopsis: A suicidal loose-cannon detective is paired with a cautious family man for a case that puts both their lives in danger and forges an unlikely friendship.
Major_Awards: $65M domestic; launched one of the most successful buddy-cop franchises; defined the genre

Title: Look Whos Talking
Synopsis: An unmarried woman's baby provides wisecracking narration as she navigates single motherhood and a budding romance with an unconventional cab driver.
Major_Awards: $140M domestic; John Travolta comeback; Bruce Willis voice; Amy Heckerling crowd-pleaser; massive 1989 hit

Title: Manhunter
Synopsis: A retired FBI profiler returns to duty to catch a serial killer and must consult the imprisoned Hannibal Lecktor to understand the murderer's mind.
Major_Awards: First screen appearance of Hannibal Lecter; Michael Mann's neo-noir masterwork; cult classic that preceded Silence of the Lambs

Title: Near Dark
Synopsis: A young Oklahoma man is turned by a beautiful vampire and must ride with a nomadic clan of bloodsuckers through the American Southwest.
Major_Awards: Kathryn Bigelow's breakthrough; cult classic that reimagined the vampire film as modern Western noir

Title: Pee-wees Big Adventure
Synopsis: Eccentric man-child Pee-wee Herman embarks on a cross-country odyssey to recover his stolen bicycle in Tim Burton's delightfully bizarre debut feature.
Major_Awards: $40M domestic on $7M budget; launched Tim Burton's career; cult classic

Title: Pixote
Synopsis: A ten-year-old boy escapes a brutal juvenile detention center in Sao Paulo and survives on the streets through petty crime and prostitution.
Major_Awards: Silver Leopard at Locarno; NY Film Critics Best Foreign Film; one of the most devastating portrayals of childhood poverty in cinema
Key_Sources: Locarno Film Festival; NY Film Critics

Title: Predator
Synopsis: An elite special forces team on a mission in Central America is hunted by a technologically advanced alien warrior in the jungle.
Major_Awards: $59M domestic; one of the defining action films of the decade; launched a major franchise

Title: Pretty in Pink
Synopsis: A working-class girl is torn between her quirky best friend and a wealthy classmate who asks her to prom in this John Hughes-penned class-conscious romance.
Major_Awards: $40M domestic; John Hughes produced/written; Molly Ringwald/Andrew McCarthy/Jon Cryer; iconic prom dress scene

Title: Re-Animator
Synopsis: A medical student develops a serum that brings the dead back to life with grotesquely unpredictable results in this gleefully gory horror-comedy.
Major_Awards: Cult classic; launched Stuart Gordon's career; one of the most celebrated horror-comedies of the decade

Title: Reckless
Synopsis: A rebellious working-class teenager and a sheltered rich girl from opposite sides of the tracks embark on a dangerous romance.
Major_Awards: James Foley feature debut; Aidan Quinn/Daryl Hannah; gritty 1980s working-class drama

Title: Risky Business
Synopsis: A suburban Chicago teenager turns his parents' house into a brothel while they're away in this sleek darkly comic satire of Reagan-era ambition.
Major_Awards: $63M domestic; launched Tom Cruise to stardom; iconic Ray-Ban scene; National Film Registry consideration

Title: Roger and Me
Synopsis: Michael Moore documents the devastating impact on Flint Michigan after General Motors closes its auto plants and lays off 30000 workers.
Major_Awards: National Film Registry; launched Michael Moore's career; NY Film Critics Best Documentary; pioneered confrontational documentary style
Key_Sources: National Film Registry; NY Film Critics

Title: Romancing the Stone
